response: The systematic use of patient-rated depression severity monitoring is indeed helpful and feasible in clinical psychiatry. According to studies, adopting measurement-based care, such as using the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), is achievable even in practices with limited resources. This approach can provide valuable insights into a patient's depressive symptoms, allowing clinicians to make more informed treatment decisions. The PHQ-9, in particular, has been shown to be a reliable tool for assessing depression severity, even in populations with vision loss. By incorporating patient-rated depression severity monitoring into clinical practice, clinicians can improve the accuracy of their diagnoses and develop more effective treatment plans for their patients.
